audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable net income is combined with 100% of CVR Partners’ D&A, capital spending, turnaround costs and working-capital movements in historical OE and the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, public common unitholders held approximately 60 % of CVR Partners’ outstanding common units; CVR Energy, through its subsidiaries, held approximately 37 % of CVR Partners’ outstanding common units and 100 % of CVR Partners’ general partner interests, while IEP held approximately 3 % of CVR Partners’ outstanding common units.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error, not merely a possible risk. Outside investors own approximately 63% of CVR Partners, and 2025 net income attributable to noncontrolling interests was $63 million versus $27 million attributable to CVR Energy. Without allocating every cash-flow adjustment consistently, the $195.9 million negative anchor represents neither consolidated equity nor CVI common equity. The net direction is mixed because excess subsidiary capex deductions can understate value while excess D&A add-backs can overstate it.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every OE year using either fully consolidated earnings and cash flows followed by an explicit noncontrolling-interest deduction, or parent-attributable earnings with each CVR Partners adjustment allocated to CVI’s economic interest; then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may give CVI holders credit for cash belonging to CVR Partners’ public unitholders
audit_findings.magnitude: $86.31 million, or approximately $0.84 per CVI share
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds consolidated cash to equity value even though approximately 63% of the $137 million of VIE cash belongs economically to outside CVR Partners unitholders.
audit_findings.evidence: We are not entitled to receive all of the cash generated by CVR Partners or freely transfer money to finance operations at the Petroleum Segment.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 filing identifies $137 million of consolidated VIE cash. Applying the filed 63% outside ownership gives an outside claim of $86.31 million. Removing it would lower base value from -$19.56 to approximately -$20.40 per share, only about 4.3% of the negative $1.998 billion base equity value and immaterial beside the $64.06-per-share gap between market price and base value. It cannot reverse the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Identify the exact CVR Partners cash balance and restrictions, replace the $737 million bridge addition with parent cash plus CVI’s attributable share of distributable subsidiary cash, and document the resulting bridge adjustment.

audit_findings.title: A cyclical turnaround outlay may have been capitalized into a perpetual negative anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $210 million filed outlay; $42.0-$52.5 million annual cycle-equivalent and $157.5-$168.0 million potential anchor over-deduction if the full outlay entered 2025 OE
audit_findings.mechanism: A four-to-five-year refinery turnaround cost may have been deducted in full from the latest-year OE anchor and then projected as an annual recurring burden.
audit_findings.evidence: The planned turnaround at the Coffeyville Refinery started in January 2025 and was completed in April 2025, with a total cash outlay of approximately $210 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes the $210 million 2025 cash outlay and a four-to-five-year refinery turnaround cycle, but the record does not establish how the valuation treated the cash outlay and related amortization. If fully deducted, normalizing it would improve the negative $195.9 million anchor by $157.5-$168.0 million. That is roughly 80%-86% of the anchor and is reasonably capable of changing the sign and scale of modeled equity value, although it would not by itself establish normalized earnings power.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $210 million outlay, the $190 million capitalized turnaround expenditure and turnaround amortization through 2025 OE; normalize one economic cost over the filed cycle without double-counting, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 numerator contains a $488 million prior-period RFS benefit unless explicitly purged
audit_findings.magnitude: $488 million pretax; after-tax OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A gain reversing RFS obligations from 2020-2024 may remain in 2025 parent-attributable earnings and therefore in the perpetual OE anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on this decision, WRC’s obligations for the 2020 through 2024 compliance periods were reduced by more than 424 million RINs, representing approximately $488 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The $488 million prior-period benefit is filed and exceeds the absolute $195.9 million OE anchor by about 2.5 times. It is not recurring 2025 operating performance. Whether it was already purged from OE is unresolved; if retained, the anchor and every scenario materially overstate value even though the reported anchor remains negative.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $488 million gain from the RFS liability and income statement into attributable net income and OE, determine its actual tax effect, remove the parent-attributable prior-period benefit while retaining ordinary current-period RFS costs, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter ignores a year-end operating conversion
audit_findings.mechanism: The latest-year OE anchor and growth cases project the former renewable-diesel configuration even though the unit reverted to hydrocarbon service in December 2025.
audit_findings.evidence: In December 2025, the Company reverted the renewable diesel unit (“RDU”) at the refinery located in Wynnewood, Oklahoma (the “Wynnewood Refinery”) back to hydrocarbon processing service, considering the unfavorable economics of the renewables business and to optimize feedstock and relieve certain logistical constraints within the refining business.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter change is demonstrated: substantially all of 2025 preceded the conversion, and 2026 reporting no longer treats renewables as a separate operating segment. The conversion’s value effect is unresolved because the discontinued renewable economics, accelerated depreciation and write-downs must be separated from the ongoing hydrocarbon margin and maintenance requirements. The direction could be positive or negative, but projecting an obsolete configuration is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Construct a same-perimeter bridge from 2025 OE to the post-conversion business, separately identifying renewable operating economics, the $93 million accelerated depreciation, the $5 million write-down and demonstrated hydrocarbon economics and maintenance needs; then rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Conditional 45Q performance obligations are an unmodeled claim ahead of equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $15 million per year and $45 million gross cap; 37% unit-share equivalent of $5.55 million per year and $16.65 million cap before tax
audit_findings.mechanism: A delivery shortfall would reduce CVR Partners’ future cash flow and distributions, lowering OE or the value attributable to CVI’s partnership interest.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the agreements entered into in connection with the 45Q Transaction, the Company’s indirect subsidiary, Coffeyville Resources Nitrogen Fertilizer, LLC (“CRNF”), is obligated to meet certain minimum quantities of carbon oxide supply each year during the term of the agreement and is subject to fees of up to $ 15 million per year (reduced pro rata for partial years) to the unaffiliated third-party investors, subject to an overall $ 45 million cap, if these minimum quantities are not delivered.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual exposure is filed, but no delivery failure, accrued liability or probable expected payment is demonstrated as of the valuation date. It is therefore a forward-looking contingency rather than a present error in OE or the bridge. If performance deteriorates, omitting the expected cost would overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Monitor annual carbon-oxide delivery against contractual minimums through 2030, obtain any shortfall notices or accruals, and model the probability-weighted parent-attributable cost when a shortfall becomes supportable.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to historical OE and could affect assessed earnings power or a future anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2022 $67.0m (23.3% of filed D&A); FY2024 $60.0m (20.1% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is conservative: unidentified D&A remains an expense and therefore cannot overstate value. The record identifies eligible add-backs of $67.0 million in 2022 and $60.0 million in 2024, but does not establish that any residual is eligible or quantify a 2025 anchor adjustment. Because the current DCF uses 2025 latest actual rather than a historical trend, the supplied 2022 and 2024 uncertainty does not directly alter the numerical scenarios; however, the record cannot establish the materiality of any analogous 2025 residual.
audit_findings.action: Obtain fixed-asset and turnaround-amortization detail for the residual D&A, classify only amounts supported as eligible add-backs, and rerun only if evidence establishes a 2025 adjustment or changes the selected anchor methodology.
